claims.statement: The proposed paid event is accepted milestone evidence and routed payment; the size and frequency of avoidable renovation disputes have not been validated for the target segment.
Owners, lenders, energy-service companies, or contractors are hypothesised to fund the fee from project budgets, but no purchase commitment or procurement route is evidenced.
Control would come from signed workflow terms with a payment provider and every project party, not from holding customer money; no such terms or integrations exist today.

The recast Energy Performance of Buildings Directive establishes renovation passports as tailored staged-renovation roadmaps, and EU digital-identity law supports electronic trust services; neither source establishes demand for this exchange.

commercial_mechanics.budget_owner: Property owner, credit or portfolio manager, project manager, or energy-service contract lead
commercial_mechanics.bundling_resistance: Stay neutral across contractors and lenders, offer reusable evidence standards, and make assessor identity and acceptance history portable
commercial_mechanics.customer_relationship_owner: Lender, energy-service company, contractor, or renovation adviser until the project parties contract directly with the exchange
commercial_mechanics.distribution_origin: Loan, renovation-passport, contractor-tender, or energy-performance-contract workflows

fully_loaded_economics.acquisition_cost: Partner integration, contractor enablement, and lender sales; target below one completed project's contribution per channel
fully_loaded_economics.cash_conversion: Platform fee captured at release; customer funds must remain with an authorised provider and outside operating cash
fully_loaded_economics.contribution_margin: Unvalidated target 30-50% after assessor and regulated-payment-partner costs
fully_loaded_economics.delivery_and_support_costs: Automated evidence collection and scheduling with human assessor work and exception-based dispute triage
fully_loaded_economics.overhead_and_compliance: Payment-services counsel, contracts, professional liability, cyber security, assessor vetting, audit logs, and accounting
fully_loaded_economics.revenue_basis: Hypothesis: 2-4% of verified milestone value with a cap, or 800-2500 PLN per assessment event
fully_loaded_economics.variable_costs: Assessor payout, payment-provider fee, identity/signature checks, evidence storage, dispute administration, and support

commercial_mechanics.likely_incumbent_response: Banks, construction-management software, energy-service companies, and payment providers may add evidence milestones to existing project products
commercial_mechanics.paid_event_or_measurable_loss: Paid event is an independently accepted project milestone and associated payment release; measurable loss is rework, delay, or dispute cost from ambiguous completion evidence
commercial_mechanics.payer: Building owner, renovation lender, energy-service company, or contractor through the project budget
commercial_mechanics.purchase_trigger: A financed or staged renovation has multiple contractors, technical milestones, or a material performance dispute risk
commercial_mechanics.renewal_event: A new project, new milestone schedule, portfolio framework renewal, or unresolved remedial inspection

contrary_evidence: Small renovation projects may prefer direct invoices and personal trust rather than a new multi-party workflow.
Existing lenders, project-management platforms, or notaries may already provide sufficient milestone control.

critical_control_point.acquisition_instrument: Proposed nonexclusive workflow-integration agreement with a regulated payment provider plus project-specific acceptance terms signed by owner, contractor, and assessor
critical_control_point.counterparty_refusal_fallback: Run evidence and electronic acceptance without holding funds, integrate a different authorised payment provider, or sell fixed-price assessor coordination outside the transaction rail
critical_control_point.current_owner: The project counterparties and their payment provider; no founder control is evidenced
critical_control_point.customer_relationship_owner: Lender, energy-service company, contractor, or renovation adviser until the project parties contract directly with the exchange
critical_control_point.duration: Proposed 24-month platform agreement; each project persists through final milestone and dispute closure
critical_control_point.founder_access_description: The founder can model evidence workflows but has no current lender, payment-provider, assessor, owner, or contractor agreement for this mechanism.
critical_control_point.launch_controller: Building owner, contractor, financier, independent assessor, and regulated payment or escrow provider
critical_control_point.renewal: Platform agreement renews annually after the initial term; project terms end on final acceptance
critical_control_point.subject: Milestone evidence, assessor assignment, counterparty sign-off, and payment-release instruction for a renovation contract

economics.acquisition_route: Channel distribution through lenders, renovation-passport experts, energy-service firms, and contractor networks
economics.founder_net_worth_path: A national evidence and payment rail could earn recurring project take rates; reaching 5m PLN would require lender or platform distribution and meaningful annual project volume over 4-7 years
economics.founder_time: Up to five hours per day if assessment is partner-delivered and only exceptions reach the founder
economics.gross_margin_basis: Fee less assessor payout, payment processing, verification, storage, support, and dispute cost
economics.payback: Target channel onboarding payback after three to six completed projects; not evidenced
economics.pricing: Hypothesis: capped 2-4% fee on accepted milestone value or 800-2500 PLN per assessment
economics.retention_or_repeat: Project milestones repeat within a renovation; portfolio partners can renew annually

fingerprint.compounding_advantage: A growing library of scoped milestones, rejection reasons, remedial actions, and final outcomes lowers dispute and assessment cost
fingerprint.customer: Owners, lenders, energy-service companies, and contractors on small commercial or multi-family renovation projects
fingerprint.distribution_mechanism: Embed at loan origination, renovation-passport preparation, contractor tender, or energy-service contracting
fingerprint.offer_and_business_model: Marketplace for standardized milestone definitions, qualified independent assessors, evidence collection, sign-off, and payment-partner routing
fingerprint.payer_and_paid_event: Project budget pays a transaction and assessment fee when a milestone evidence packet is accepted and payment is released
fingerprint.problem_trigger: A staged renovation needs an objective release decision before the owner or financier pays the next milestone

founder_fit: Business-analysis and data skills suit structured acceptance rules, anomaly detection, and unit economics
The mechanism can become workflow software with scheduled assessor capacity rather than founder-led site work
A no-funds-held pilot can stay within 100k PLN and avoid premature balance-sheet exposure
Renewable-sector familiarity helps define an initial renovation scope without relying on confidential resources
risks: Any accidental custody or control of client funds could trigger material regulation
Conflicts among owner, contractor, assessor, and lender can create costly manual disputes
Low renovation frequency may make marketplace liquidity difficult
An incumbent lender or construction platform can bundle the rail

structural_signature.commercial_model_descriptor: take rate and booking fee on independently accepted renovation milestones
structural_signature.control_point_descriptor: evidence signature and payment routing workflow at each milestone release
structural_signature.critical_dependency_descriptor: qualified independent assessors accepted by all project counterparties

structure.control_point: the evidence-and-sign-off transaction rail before project funds are released
structure.critical_dependency: available independent assessors who are accepted by owners, contractors, and funders

thesis: Future operating state (2032): small-building renovations are financed and paid through measured milestones rather than one final contractor invoice. Missing contractual and coordination mechanism: a neutral acceptance workflow that binds scoped evidence, an independent assessor, electronic sign-off, and a regulated payment or escrow partner to each release event.
title: Renovation Acceptance Exchange
uncertainties: Whether Polish owners and lenders will accept standardized remote evidence for fund release
Which assessment activities require licensed professionals or accredited methods
Payment-services and escrow classification when the platform initiates or conditions releases
Assessor supply density and dispute rate at viable transaction fees
